summary: substr extracts text using one-based positions.
documentation: substr extracts text using one-based positions. A negative start counts backward from the end. For text, positions refer to characters rather than UTF-8 bytes; NULL arguments yield NULL.
inputs: Text, a start position and optional length.
caution: SQLite positions begin at 1. Negative length has its own backwards-selection meaning; do not confuse it with a negative start.
scenarios: Display the tail of an internal reference in a compact report.
Extract fixed-position portions of a documented import format.
Show a shortened code while keeping the full value stored.
title: Display reference tails
problem: From references_list(id INTEGER, code TEXT), return id and substr(code, -4) as tail, ordered by id. Short strings remain whole, empty strings remain empty, and NULL remains NULL.
goal: Use substr() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Start four characters back from the end and omit length.
